messages:
alex: Hey, hitting a weird install failure when users pip install the latest python-sdk wheel from our package index. Works for me locally but CI and a couple of customer reports fail with a typing-related error.

alex: Error snippet from a failing VM:```ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement typing_extensions<5,>=4.0 (from our-sdk==0.9.1)```

sam: Is that from pip install or from poetry?

alex: pip install of the built wheel. The wheel was built by our GH action (poetry build -> twine upload).

lina: Do we have typing_extensions pinned in pyproject extras or main deps? I thought we relaxed it recently.

alex: pyproject shows: `typing-extensions = "^4.1.0"` — poetry resolves it to 4.8 on some envs, but on others pip tries to pick 5.x? The error looks like something in the wheel METADATA requiring <5.

brian: Could be our build tooling adding an extra marker. Also saw pip on py3.12 treat typing-extensions differently because it's in stdlib for some parts. Maybe the constraint needs to be conditional on python_version.

sam: Also: CI logs show the wheel filename is `our_sdk-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl` — not manylinux tagged. Some linux customers hit issues installing that wheel on older pip. Could be that the wheel is missing compiled extension tags or a platform mismatch.

alex: Hmm, the package is pure python (no compiled ext). Why would manylinux matter? One user on Debian 10 reported pip trying to compile something.

lina: Could be that cibuildwheel wasn't used so the wheel isn't built with the expected universal tags. If pip deems it incompatible it falls fallback to sdist which triggers build on install and then fails due to build deps.

brian: Related: our GH action uses `poetry build` which produces a wheel but not necessarily universal. We should run cibuildwheel to generate manylinux wheels for linux. That would reduce sdist fallbacks.

sam: Also, what does our pyproject.lock (poetry.lock) look like? If users install via pip, they don't use our lockfile. But our build might be embedding requires with strict pins into METADATA.

alex: I attached minimal pip output in the ticket:```
Processing /tmp/pip-install-XXXX/our-sdk
  Preparing metadata (pyproject.toml) ... error
  error: subprocess-exited-with-error
  × Preparing metadata (pyproject.toml) did not run successfully.
  │ exit code: 1
  ╰─> See above for output.
  note: This error originates from a subprocess, and is likely not a problem with pip.
```

lina: That matches sdist->PEP517 build path failing. When poetry build -> wheel works locally, but pip install from index sometimes gets sdist if wheel incompatible. So first action: generate proper manylinux wheels via cibuildwheel and publish.

brian: Second action: relax typing-extensions constraint or make it conditional. Example in pyproject: `typing-extensions = {version = "^4.1.0", markers = "python_version < '3.12'"}` — so py3.12 won't pull the backport.

sam: We should also ensure our package metadata doesn't vendor a pinned typing-extensions in install_requires; poetry might be converting caret pins to exact pins in the built wheel depending on version. Which poetry version did the action use?

alex: GH action uses `poetry-core 1.6.1` last time I checked. The lockfile is checked into repo but on build we don't pass the lock to `pip` so metadata uses ranges. Not sure how exacts get embedded.

lina: Another quick workaround: add a pyproject.toml [tool.poetry.dependencies] entry with env markers as brian suggested, run clean build, and try installing wheel in a clean pyenv for 3.11/3.12.

brian: We should also update CI matrix to test install via pip on multiple interpreters (3.9/3.10/3.11/3.12) and on a linux runner that uses older pip to replicate customer environments. Add a test that does `pip install our-sdk==0.9.1 --index-url <staging>` then import and run a simple call.

alex: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to: 1) add cibuildwheel build job, 2) relax typing-extensions pin with python_version marker, 3) add install-via-pip smoke test in CI.

sam: Can we also confirm editable/install workflow for devs? A few folks had trouble with `poetry install --no-root` vs `pip install -e .` after the editable PEP changes. Might be another source of friction for contributors.

lina: Good call. Add a note in CONTRIBUTING.md with recommended dev setup: `poetry install --with dev`, or `pip install -e '.[dev]'` depending on preference. Also mention `poetry export -f requirements.txt --output requirements-dev.txt` for envs that need pip.

brian: I can take the CI matrix changes. alex you take the cibuildwheel + pyproject tweak. lina can update contributing docs.

alex: Starting the PR now. I'll link the branch here when ready.

pkg-bot: Created issue #4572 for "wheel build + typing-extensions compatibility on py3.12" and assigned alex, brian, lina.

alex: Thanks all — will follow up with PR link and rough ETA (couple hours). If anyone else saw the exact pip error from customers please drop it here.
